scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W008 (Scrimshaw1): The anchor image confirms a single heavy blue contour line dominates; the zigzag teeth at the lower jaw and scribbled oval hollows are visible. The soft lavender/yellow circles in the background are confirmed. The description 'barely holding itself together' is psychological inference and has been softened to a visible observation about the contrast between the loose background and the jagged foreground line.

W017 (Scrimshaw4): The sky-blue background and floating head built from purple arcs are confirmed. The doubled mouth (two tooth rows) is visible. The phrase 'arrived before its surroundings could fill in' implies chronology and has been removed.

W026 (Scrimshaw9): The salmon-pink background, overlapping purple/blue contour lines, and the spiral vortex at center-left are confirmed. The diagonal hatching bleeding into the figure edges is visible. The word 'frantic' is a possible reading grounded in visible density of marks—retained as possibility.

W004 (Scrimshaw8): The image confirms a long face and narrow neck against a purple field, white loops for eyes and mouth, and an additional oval on the forehead with a yellow loop above. The description is accurate and restrained.
W016 (Scrimshaw6): The tilted warm-colored head against bright yellow, blue loops for eyes and nose, and broad translucent orange/pink/brown areas are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W001 (Scrimshaw6): The large head on green ground, thick red/black/yellow lines, differently framed eyes (purple ring vs orange loops), and rows of yellow/blue oval mouth marks are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W003 (Scrimshaw 18): The rectangular scaffolding, asymmetric eyes, orbiting loops, and orange background are confirmed. The phrase 'mechanical quality' is an interpretive claim softened to 'constructed quality' grounded in the visible rectangular shapes.
W006 (Scrimshaw 21): The tilted head on yellow ground, angular multicolored strokes, and long marks fanning outward above the head are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W007 (Scrimshaw 40): The white X over the right side of the face, the red oval mouth with jagged yellow-green teeth, and the flat gray field are confirmed. The lime-green/yellow hatching at the crown is visible. The reading 'cancellation or wound' is retained as a possibility grounded in the visible X mark.

W010 (Wobbler): The three eye-like forms (diamond on forehead, broad blue oval, rounded blue frame), the dark horizontal mouth with vertical bars, and the warm yellow/orange crown marks are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W011 (Scrimshaw8): The small elongated face within a wide spread of black/pink/turquoise strands on bright yellow is confirmed. The forehead oval and ordinary eye pair are visible. Description is accurate.

W005 (Scrimshaw13): The frontal face with mismatched spiral eyes, wide dark oval top, red-outlined mouth with zigzag teeth, and small secondary circle below the chin are confirmed. The pale yellow-green wash is visible. Description is accurate.

W014 (Scrimshaw14): The large face on saturated yellow, asymmetric spiral eyes (one loose/layered, one tight bullseye), zigzag forehead lines, and gaping toothed mouth are confirmed. The phrase 'scream caught mid-breath' is an emotional inference; softened to 'the open mouth and taut forehead lines hold the expression unresolved.'

W018 (Scrimshaw7): The anchor image confirms the pink-lavender spiral at upper-left of the head, radiating dark/red/gray lines fanning outward, two large oval eyes with concentric rings, the vertical teal stripe down the center, and the jagged white triangular teeth. The description 'alarm or confrontation' is retained as a possibility grounded in the bared teeth and radiating lines. The claim 'face caught mid-shout' is softened.

W012 (Scrimshaw15): The face with radiating red/yellow/orange/blue streaks, the bright blue background at corners, and the pale yellow-green interior wash are confirmed. The phrase 'feverish' is retained as a possibility grounded in the warm interior against cool ground. 'Scream caught mid-breath' is a repeated stock phrase from W014 and has been removed and replaced.

W019 (Scrimshaw5): The skull-like head on saturated yellow, layered loop construction, mismatched eyes (cross-mark vs dark spiral), row of pointed teeth, and chain-like blue-gray loops at the bottom are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W009 (Scrimshaw 41): The three concentric spiral circles for eye sockets, dense black scribble over warm olive-gold washes, black background, and white zigzag teeth above a red-orange bar are confirmed. The phrase 'menacing or mournful' is retained as a possibility grounded in the contrast between dark mass and warm glow.

W021 (Scrimshaw 24): The white X over the left eye, the looser right eye spiral, the barred mouth, and the purple scribbles spilling into the lavender-purple background are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W020 (Scrimshaw 42): The profile skull on black ground, layered neon outlines in pink/yellow/cyan/red, the jagged yellow crown at upper right, and the mismatched eye spirals are confirmed. The description 'vibrate against the black field' is grounded in the visible offset color passes.

W002 (Scrimshaw 33): The two profile heads facing right on near-black background, the dense interior color tangles, and the coral-pink projection from the left head into the gap are confirmed. The left head tilting slightly upward and the right jutting forward are visible. Description is accurate.

W024 (Scrimshaw3): The three black-outlined heads, the dense orange/teal/blue/red/pink underlayer, and the bold white scrawled marks crossing the middle zone are confirmed. The description 'spoken over or half-erased' is retained as a possibility grounded in the white marks obscuring features.

W023 (Scrimshaw12): The roughly four-by-four grid of rounded rectangular face compartments, the saturated purple-violet background with orange/yellow/white/pink streaks, and the varied fill colors per cell are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W015 (Scrimshaw2): The concentric oval loops in blue/teal/yellow at upper-left, the zigzag marks in the lower rectangular region, and the pale vertical/wavy lines running down both sides over a saturated blue field are confirmed. The description is accurate. The claim 'skull-like arrangement' is a possible reading grounded in the two hollow shapes and the zigzag marks below.

W022 (Trio1): The three narrow upright figures on warm orange field, the red/blue/white/yellow lines forming angular bodies and oval heads, and the radiating side marks are confirmed. The larger oval above the middle figure is visible. Description is accurate.

W013 (Stick Together): The five upright figures side by side, the long colored body regions, the thin crossing lines, and the looped white/yellow marks above the heads are confirmed. Description is accurate.

W025 (GM): The anchor image confirms two large letterforms G and M filling the composition. The G contains concentric curved loops with a nested rectangular shape filled by warm yellow/pink scribbles. The M splays outward with cyan/yellow/magenta strokes. The loose border of scrawled lines and the flat muted background blocks (olive, dark purple, ochre) are confirmed. The description 'flickering, almost neon quality' is grounded in the visible competing warm/cool strokes. The claim about 'inner loops of the G echo the spiral eyes' is a visible correspondence and is retained.

Chapter pacing: Five chapters provide opening/development/contrast/closing arc. Chapter 3 ('The Face Under Maximum Pressure') begins with W011 as a deliberate pullback before re-escalating—this is a valid contrast move but the chapter introduction has been clarified to reflect this.

Repeated language: 'scream caught mid-breath' appeared in both W014 and W012 readings; corrected in W012. 'Feverish' in W012 is retained as a single use. 'Unresolved' appears multiple times but describes genuinely different visible features each time—retained with varied phrasing where possible.

W015 placement: W015 is placed as a bridge between the grid chapter and the final chapter. Its role as a single face dissolving toward pattern is a valid contrasting function grounded in the visible vertical lines and loop structure.
No invented objects, no unsupported chronology, no artist psychology claims remain after corrections.
W018 reading previously claimed 'clashing yellows, pinks, and blues'—the anchor image confirms yellow, pink/lavender, and blue/teal are all present. Claim is accurate.
W025: The draft described 'flat muted blocks—olive, dark purple, ochre' behind the linework. The anchor image confirms these muted color blocks are present. Accurate.
evidence.limitation: Ensemble sheet review and three original anchors; not full-resolution individual inspection of every work or a visitor study
evidence.wordingReviewScope: Text-only tightening of image-reviewed headings and invitations; no new image inspection or membership change
evidence.assistantWordingScope: Specificity and overstatement corrections to exhibition headings and invitations. Existing image-reviewed memberships, chapter order and artwork roles remain intact.
evidence.referenceExpansionMethod: Exact collection-plan slot to title and CID lookup; no new interpretation
canvasFindings: W002 Scrimshaw 33: The background is near-black (very dark maroon), not a neutral or warm field. The two heads are densely packed with vivid overlapping color tangles—purple, red, coral, teal, yellow—set against this dark surround, which makes the forms read as luminous rather than hollow. The coral projection is clearly visible as a looping pink-red form descending from the left head into the gap. The word 'hollow-looking' misrepresents the actual dense, color-filled interiors.

W004 Scrimshaw8: The background is a bright, saturated violet-purple field with warm orange and red horizontal slashes cutting across it. The face is heavily layered with dark scribbled strands (olive, dark gray, black) over which white, red, and yellow marks define features. The forehead carries a warm orange halo-like arc. The description of 'white loops' for features is partially accurate but undersells the density of dark scribble and the vivid purple-red-orange surround. The neck is not especially prominent as a downward pull; the face fills the frame with dense mark-making rather than a long-neck vertical tension.

W005 Scrimshaw13: The background is a soft yellow-green with pale vertical washes, not a plain field. The face fills most of the frame with dense overlapping lines. The spiral eyes are clearly present—one red-dominant, one darker with a cross-like mark inside. The open toothed mouth is visible. A small secondary teal circle sits below the chin. The hat-like oval at the top is a prominent black scribble ring. The description is broadly accurate but the background color (yellow-green with pale vertical bands) was likely darkened in the old conversion.

W007 Scrimshaw 40: The background is a flat medium gray. The face is densely packed with vivid color blocks—yellow, teal, blue, green, pink—under heavy black scribble. A white X sits over the right eye area. The mouth is open with a pink surround and white zigzag teeth. A bright green scribble erupts from the top. A purple outline frames the head. The old description called the field 'flat gray' which is correct, but described the figure as relatively spare; in fact the face interior is extremely dense with color and black overscribble, not a simple colored-block face.

W012 Scrimshaw15: The background is a bright sky blue at the corners and edges, with warm yellow, red, and orange hair-like strokes radiating outward from the face in all directions. The face interior is yellow with blue and black contour loops. A purple mouth with visible teeth anchors the lower face. Red and orange strands dominate the upper and side regions. The old description mentioned 'cool blue ground at the corners' which is correct, but 'warm yellows and reds inside the face' is accurate. The overall image is brighter and more saturated than the old conversion suggested.

W013 Stick Together: The background is a pale aqua-teal rectangle framed by a thin black border, with a warm peach-tan band below. Five figures stand in a row, each with a distinct color body (yellow, teal, pink-mauve, purple). Faces are rendered with colored scribble marks (purple, green, red, teal). Loops above heads are visible as white oval scribbles in the upper background. The crossing lines between figures are present but relatively sparse—thin black lines. The description of 'thin lines crossing between them' is accurate. The background is light and airy, not dark.

W015 Scrimshaw2: The image is dominated by blue—a rich, saturated blue field with teal, white, and gray loop forms building the face. The large spiral on the left side of the face is prominent. The mouth is open with white zigzag teeth on a teal ground. Vertical lines are present as pale blue-white strands hanging below the face. The description of 'pale vertical lines' is accurate but the overall ground is strongly blue, not described as such in the existing prose. The face is not dissolving into pattern so much as constructed entirely from blue-family loops with yellow accents.

W016 Scrimshaw6: The background is a flat, saturated yellow. The face is rendered with soft peach-pink washes for the flesh, blue loops for eye and chin contours, dark brown-red scribble for hair radiating outward, and red accent marks. The face is relatively open and readable compared to denser works. The description of 'broad orange and pink masses' overstates the orange; the flesh tones are more peach-pink and the dominant surround is yellow. 'Fine blue loops keep its edges unsettled' is accurate.

W018 Scrimshaw7: The background is a warm yellow field at center with teal-blue and lavender at the edges. Radiating pink-red and dark strands fill the upper portion. A pink-lavender spiral sits prominently on the forehead. The face has a teal vertical stripe down the nose. Eyes are rendered with layered loops. The mouth is open with white zigzag teeth. The description of 'pink-lavender spiral crown' is accurate. 'Teal stripe splits the face' is accurate. The background is warm yellow rather than neutral, and the radiating strands are more pink-red than previously described.

W023 Scrimshaw12: The purple ground is correct and clearly visible between and around the cells. Each face cell has a distinct fill—some purple, some green-gray, some yellow, some multicolored. Black grid lines and yellow scribble overlay the whole surface. White marks appear on several faces. The description of 'purple ground pushes warmer fills forward' is accurate. The grid reads as roughly four-by-four. No significant correction needed beyond confirming the purple is vivid and the cell fills are varied rather than uniformly warm.

W026 Scrimshaw9: The background is a warm salmon-pink field. The face is rendered with yellow-green and teal washes for the flesh, blue and purple line work for contours, and cyan and white slashing strokes across the upper head. A blue-purple spiral sits in the left eye socket area. The description of 'spiral vortex reads as an eye socket' and 'slashing cyan lines scatter attention outward' is accurate. The 'salmon field' description is correct. The face reads more as a three-quarter view tilted downward than a frontal face.
evidence.canvasComposition: Original source alpha correctly composited over original white drawing canvas

title: Scrimshaw: Faces, Figures and Letters
question: What connects the overlapping lines in a portrait, a group of figures and lettering?
introduction: Follow facial contours through increasingly layered heads, then compare doubled forms, grouped figures and lettering. Colored lines can describe an eye or mouth while also forming a pattern across the surface. The final standing figures and the letters in GM offer a concrete comparison with earlier portraits, while keeping their different subjects clear.
closing: Compare the edges of the letters in GM with a contour in an earlier portrait. How do overlapping lines describe these two different subjects?

chapters.title: One Contour Does the Work
chapters.introduction: Three works open with faces where a single dominant line—blue, purple, or warm orange—carries the structure, while softer marks occupy the space around or behind it. The first two sit against open, lightly colored grounds; the third presses the face into a dense violet field.

stops.whyHere: A single heavy blue line carves the face; soft lavender and yellow circles behind it contrast with the jagged foreground, making the contour feel exposed rather than settled.
stops.title: Scrimshaw1

stops.whyHere: Purple arcs replace the blue contour; the head floats against open sky-blue with more bare ground visible, the boundary between figure and field already loosening.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use one dominant color to trace the head, but here far more empty ground surrounds the form, making the face feel less anchored.
stops.title: Scrimshaw4

stops.whyHere: A face dense with dark scribbled strands—olive, gray, and black—fills the frame against a bright violet-purple field slashed with warm orange and red arcs; white and red marks pick out features beneath the layered tangle, and the saturated surround holds the whole under pressure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous head floats freely against open ground, this face is buried under dense overlapping strands, the vivid purple field pressing inward rather than releasing the form.
stops.title: Scrimshaw8

chapters.title: No Single Line Governs
chapters.introduction: Seven works layer overlapping strokes across the face until color, asymmetry, and repetition share the surface equally, with no one mark settling the whole. Grounds range from warm salmon and saturated yellow to flat gray, each shaping how much pressure the layered marks exert.

stops.whyHere: A blue-purple spiral marks the eye socket of a three-quarter face tilted downward; yellow-green and teal flesh washes underlie blue and purple contour lines while cyan and white slashing strokes scatter across the upper head, all held within a warm salmon-pink field that absorbs the collision without resolving it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The single governing contour of the previous chapter dissolves here into competing colored lines and slashing strokes pressing against a warm, unbroken salmon ground.
stops.title: Scrimshaw9

stops.whyHere: Soft peach-pink flesh washes and blue contour loops give the tilted face a readable volume against a flat saturated yellow ground; dark brown-red hair scribble radiates outward and red accent marks keep the edges unsettled without overwhelming the open center.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a warm field to contain a tangled head, but this face is more open and its peach-pink flesh tones lighter, the marks spreading outward rather than pressing inward.
stops.title: Scrimshaw6

stops.whyHere: Thick red, black, and yellow lines crowd a large head; differently framed eyes and rows of oval mouth-marks briefly steady an otherwise dense surface.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The warm-field looseness of the previous work tightens here: the head nearly fills the square and the marks grow heavier and more insistent.
stops.title: Scrimshaw6

stops.whyHere: Rectangular scaffolding in red and blue holds soft pink fills; orbiting purple and yellow loops extend past the head into the orange field, giving the face a constructed, pressurized quality.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a yellow-orange ground and crowded marks, but this head introduces rigid rectangular shapes that make the face feel built rather than drawn.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 18

stops.whyHere: Long strokes fan outward above the tilted head, carrying the face's restless energy into the surrounding yellow space beyond the skull's edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The orbiting loops of the previous work become directional here: marks escape upward and outward rather than circling the form.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 21

stops.whyHere: A face packed with vivid color blocks—yellow, teal, blue, green, pink—under dense black overscribble sits against a flat gray field; a white X marks one eye area, a pink-rimmed open mouth shows white zigzag teeth, and a bright green scribble erupts from the crown.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The bright yellow ground gives way to flat gray, and the face interior, though densely colored, is pressed under heavy black scribble that makes the X-mark and open mouth feel like the only points of clarity.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 40

stops.whyHere: Three eye-like forms at different heights give the face an unsteady gaze; vertical bars across the mouth make the expression harder to settle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The single X-mark of the previous work expands here into three competing eye forms, multiplying the points of uncertainty across the face.
stops.title: Wobbler

chapters.title: Accumulation at Its Densest
chapters.introduction: Seven works push mark-making furthest, opening with one deliberate reduction before re-escalating. Spiral eyes, bared teeth, and radiating lines make the face a site of layered addition rather than a stable image.

stops.whyHere: A small elongated face sits within a wide spread of colored strands; the contrast between narrow head and expansive surroundings gives the portrait a different scale at each stage of looking.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After the crowded, nearly full-frame faces, this work pulls back: the head shrinks inside its own hair-like field, reversing the pressure before it builds again.
stops.title: Scrimshaw8

stops.whyHere: Mismatched spiral eyes—one red-dominant, one darker with a cross-like interior—and an open toothed mouth stare outward from a yellow-green ground with pale vertical washes; a black scribble ring crowns the head and a small teal circle below the chin suggests the face is still accumulating downward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works show a face surrounded by tangled strands, but here the head reasserts its full-frame scale, the spiral eyes lock the gaze, and the pale vertical ground replaces the expansive hair-like field.
stops.title: Scrimshaw13

stops.whyHere: One eye is loose and layered, the other a tight bullseye; zigzag lines across the forehead and a gaping toothed mouth leave the expression unresolved against the bright yellow field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The spiral eyes of the previous work reappear here in a more extreme asymmetry, and the yellow ground intensifies the sense of forward pressure.
stops.title: Scrimshaw14

stops.whyHere: A pink-lavender spiral sits prominently on the forehead while pink-red and dark strands radiate outward through the warm yellow field; a teal stripe runs down the nose dividing the face vertically, and an open mouth with white zigzag teeth anchors the lower half against lavender and blue edges.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The bullseye eye of the previous work becomes a full forehead spiral here, the warm yellow center surrounded by radiating pink-red strands, and the face divides vertically rather than varying eye by eye.
stops.title: Scrimshaw7

stops.whyHere: Red, orange, and yellow hair-like strokes radiate outward in every direction from a yellow face with blue and black contour loops; a purple-rimmed mouth with visible teeth anchors the center while a bright blue field at the corners frames the outward dispersal.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The radiating lines that escaped upward in earlier works now push simultaneously in every direction, and the blue ground at the edges gives the dispersal a cooler frame that sharpens the warm interior.
stops.title: Scrimshaw15

stops.whyHere: Layered loops construct a head that reads as both face and skull; chain-like forms at the bottom leave the figure's mood between restraint and ornament.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use a hot yellow field and tangled reds, but this face introduces skull-like exposed teeth and chain forms that shift the register toward something more structural.
stops.title: Scrimshaw5

stops.whyHere: Three hollow spiral sockets stare with unsettling symmetry; warm golden tones seep through dense black scribble, giving the dark mass a faint glow that can read as either menacing or mournful.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The skull reading of the previous work intensifies here: the black ground and three symmetrical sockets make this the most mask-like and confrontational face in the sequence.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 41

chapters.title: One Face Becomes Several
chapters.introduction: Six works place more than one face in the same image—through split halves, paired profiles, three crowded heads, and a full grid—testing whether repetition clarifies or dissolves the subject.

stops.whyHere: A white X seals one eye while the other stays open; purple scribbles spill past the face into the background, dissolving the boundary between figure and field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The three-socket symmetry of the previous work breaks here: one side of the face is marked through, giving the two halves different weight.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 24

stops.whyHere: Layered neon outlines trace a skull in profile, each color pass slightly offset so the form appears to shift; a jagged crown reads as another restless loop rather than decoration.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The frontal face gives way to a profile, and the single-pass outline multiplies into layered offsets that make the skull appear to vibrate.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 42

stops.whyHere: Two densely color-filled heads face the same direction against a near-black ground; vivid purple, red, teal, and yellow tangles pack each form, and a looping coral projection from the left head reaches into the dark gap without bridging the two.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The single profile of the previous work doubles here, but the two heads remain isolated despite their closeness, the near-black ground deepening the gap between them rather than letting it breathe.
stops.title: Scrimshaw 33

stops.whyHere: Three black-outlined heads crowd the frame; white scrawl layered across their faces obscures mouths and eyes, lending the group a feeling of being partially erased.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two isolated profiles become three heads pressed shoulder to shoulder, and a new layer of white marks partially covers the features just established.
stops.title: Scrimshaw3

stops.whyHere: A roughly four-by-four grid boxes each face into its own cell with varied fills—purple, green-gray, yellow, multicolored—against a vivid purple ground; black grid lines and yellow scribble overlay the whole surface so that every face competes equally and none can hold the eye alone.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Three heads become a grid of many, the vivid purple ground formalizing the crowd into cells where the varied fills surface faces from noise without letting any single one settle.
stops.title: Scrimshaw12

stops.whyHere: A rich blue field built entirely from looping teal, white, and gray strokes constructs the face; a large spiral dominates one side, an open mouth with white zigzag teeth anchors the lower half, and pale blue-white strands hang below, pulling the face toward pure loop-pattern.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The grid's many cells compress back into a single face, but the saturated blue ground and continuous looping lines dissolve its edges toward pattern, bridging the crowd and the figures that follow.
stops.title: Scrimshaw2

chapters.title: Figures and Letters Replace the Face
chapters.introduction: Three final works move away from the isolated portrait: figures stand in groups, and two large letters occupy the space where a single face appeared throughout.

stops.whyHere: Three narrow figures share an orange field; radiating side marks and a hovering oval above the central figure give the group a shared structure without merging it into one body.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The dissolving single face of the previous work gives way to three distinct upright figures, restoring bodily presence but distributing it across a group.
stops.title: Trio1

stops.whyHere: Five figures stand in a row against a pale aqua background, each body a distinct color column—yellow, teal, pink-mauve, purple; colored scribble marks differentiate each face while white oval loops above the heads repeat across the group, and sparse crossing lines between bodies hold togetherness and separateness in the same open field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Three figures become five, the light airy ground replacing the orange field of the previous work, and the crossing lines between bodies remain sparse enough that each figure keeps its own color identity within the shared row.
stops.title: Stick Together

stops.whyHere: Two large letters built from layered colored strokes occupy the space where a face would be; the inner loops of the G echo the spiral eye forms seen throughout the exhibition.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The five standing figures give way to two letters that use the same overlapping mark language as every face in the show, asking whether the greeting replaces or simply is a face.
stops.title: GM
